title: Helical and Straight Solitons Induced by Vortex Beams with Off-Axis Pivots in Cubic-Quintic Nonlinear Media
authors: Jing Chen, Rongcao Yang, Boris A. Malomed
abstract: We address the existence and dynamics of solitons propagating along helical (spiral-rotating) and straight trajectories in the bulk waveguide with the cubic-quintic nonlinearity and a single- or multi-ring potential. The input is taken as a vortex beam with a single or multiple phase singularities (pivots), displaced from the waveguide's axis. The single off-axis pivot creates a one-ring helical soliton, with a closed or open (split) ring structure. The vortex beams with multiple off-center pivots give rise to complex states with multi-ring, multi-core, and/or multi-split structures. The multi-core/split solitons propagate along helical channels, or straight ones, which are parallel to the propagation axis. The sign and period of the helicity can be precisely adjusted by applying a torque with an appropriate angular velocity.
summary: This paper theoretically examines complex soliton solutions—specifically helical and straight multi-core structures—formed by vortex beams propagating in a cubic-quintic nonlinear medium. By analyzing the impact of off-axis phase singularities and applying external torques, the authors demonstrate precise control over the soliton's structure and propagation characteristics. This is significant for understanding advanced light manipulation in nonlinear optical systems.
main_problem: The study investigates the existence and dynamics of solitons propagating along helical and straight trajectories induced by vortex beams with off-axis pivots in cubic-quintic nonlinear media.
main_result: The research predicts stable multi-ring, multi-core, and/or multi-split soliton structures, demonstrating that the helicity and propagation channels can be precisely tuned by applying an external torque.
method: The analysis involves solving the nonlinear Schrödinger equation numerically, utilizing linear stability analysis (eigenvalue problems) to confirm stability, and analyzing energy flow via the Poynting vector.
model_or_system: The system models optical beams propagating in a cubic-quintic (CQ) nonlinear medium, characterized by a single- or multi-ring potential. The dynamics are governed by the Nonlinear Schrödinger Equation (NLSE) incorporating the effects of off-axis vortex beam pivots.
key_observables: Soliton structure (multi-ring, multi-core, split), helicity sign/period, linear eigenvalue spectra, and energy flow density.
important_parameters: Potential depth ($V_0$), propagation constant ($ eta$), topological charge ($m$), and applied angular velocity ($\Omega$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the validity of the CQ nonlinearity model and relies on solving the linearized eigenvalue problem for stability assessment.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the concentric ring potentials, the field amplitude and Poynting vector for off-axis solitons, comparisons of power and stability for on-axis vs. off-axis states, and the field patterns under applied rotation.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by establishing the governing NLSE, analyzing the effect of off-axis pivots on single-ring solitons, extending the analysis to multi-ring potentials, and finally demonstrating the co-existence and tunability of helical and straight propagation channels via external torque.
why_interesting: This work bridges nonlinear optics and soliton physics, providing detailed theoretical predictions about complex, structured light beams (vortex solitons) whose dynamics are controlled by geometric parameters (off-axis pivots) and external forces (torque).
